title: A 1-Year Weight Management Program for Difficult-to-Treat Asthma With Obesity: A Randomized Controlled Study
authors: Sharma V, Ricketts HC, McCombie L, Brosnahan N, Crawford L, Slaughter L, et al.
population: Adults with difficult-to-treat asthma and BMI 30 kg/m² or more in Glasgow; Counterweight-Plus programme (12-week 850 kcal/day total diet replacement, then food reintroduction and maintenance) against usual care, 1:1
funder: The trial was sponsored and funded by an NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde Endowment Fund; contributors to the funding had no input into design, conduct, analysis, interpretation or writing.
authorConflicts: One author is an employee and shareholder of Counterweight Ltd, which provides the programme, delivered the intervention with others and contributed to data interpretation; another author is a medical advisor for Counterweight Ltd and has received fees from Novo Nordisk and Nestlé; others report fees from AstraZeneca, GSK and other companies.
result: 29 of 36 participants attended at 52 weeks (13 programme, 16 usual care). Median weight change was -14 kg (IQR -15 to -9) against 2 kg (-7 to 8). More participants reached the minimal clinically important improvement in AQLQ with the programme (71% against 6%), whereas ACQ-6 change did not differ between groups (mean difference 0.4, 95% CI -0.5 to 1.2). Median annual courses of high-dose oral corticosteroid fell from 4 to 0 within the programme group, without a between-group difference. Seventy percent of the programme group lost 10% of weight or more.
